cards.text: Here's where we are, friend. Haman, the king's top official, got King Xerxes to seal a decree: on one single day, the thirteenth of Adar, every Jew in the kingdom is to be destroyed (Esther 3:13). And now Mordecai, the Jew who wouldn't bow to Haman (Esther 3:2), learns of all that had happened.

cards.question: Mordecai has just learned about the decree against all the Jews. What does he do?

answers.text: He tears his clothes and puts on sackcloth
He goes straight to Haman's house to argue
He locks himself inside his home to hide

cards.text: Then Mordecai goes out into the middle of the city, wailing loudly and bitterly. This is not a quiet sniffle in the corner, friend. This is LOUD, right in the middle of town.

cards.question: Mordecai, still in his sackcloth, goes only as far as the king's gate. Why does he stop there?

answers.text: The law kept anyone in sackcloth out
The guards were under Haman's orders
Esther had told him to wait right there

cards.text: Meanwhile, the king's command is reaching every province. And Mordecai is not the only one taking it hard.

cards.question: The king's decree reaches the Jews in every province. How do they respond?

answers.text: They fast and weep and lament
They gather together to fight back
They pack up and leave the kingdom

cards.text: Over in the palace, Esther's maidens and eunuchs come and tell her about Mordecai. Esther is the queen, and Mordecai is the cousin who took her in as his own daughter (Esther 2:7).

cards.question: Queen Esther is overcome with distress about Mordecai. What does she send out to him?

answers.text: Clothes to wear instead of sackcloth
A palace guard to keep him safe
A message telling him to go home

cards.question: Mordecai takes the clothes Esther sent and changes out of his sackcloth.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Mordecai won't accept them. So Esther summons Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs appointed to her, and dispatches him out to Mordecai.

cards.question: Queen Esther sends Hathach out to Mordecai. What does she want Hathach to find out?

answers.text: What is troubling Mordecai and why
Whether Haman can still be trusted
When the king plans to call for her

cards.text: Hathach finds Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate. And Mordecai tells him all that has happened to him.

cards.question: Mordecai even tells Hathach the exact amount of money Haman promised to pay into the royal ___ to destroy the Jews.

answers.text: treasury
army
court

cards.question: Mordecai doesn't just talk to Hathach. He hands him something to show and explain to Esther. What is it?

answers.text: A copy of the written decree
The king's own signet ring
A letter from Haman himself

cards.question: Mordecai sends Hathach back with a request for Queen Esther. What does he urge her to do?

answers.text: Go to the king and plead for her people
Leave Susa before the day of the decree
Ask Haman to change his mind about it

cards.text: So Hathach goes back and relays everything Mordecai said to Esther. Friend, Hathach is the whole palace group chat, and he is WALKING every single message.
Hathach, lace those sandals back up, buddy, because Esther has an answer for Mordecai. And her answer starts with a law everybody in the kingdom knows.

cards.question: Esther says one law applies to anyone who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned. What does it say happens to them?

answers.text: They are put to death
They are sent out of Susa
They lose every royal title

cards.question: Esther says a person who goes to the king unsummoned has only one way to live. What must the king do?

answers.text: Hold out his gold scepter
Hand over his signet ring
Stand up from his throne

cards.question: Esther adds that she has not been summoned to appear before the king for the past ___ days.

answers.text: thirty
seven
forty

cards.text: Thirty days without a call from the king. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to reach in for me, so trust me, friend, I know a thing or two about waiting to get called.
Esther's words are relayed to Mordecai. And Mordecai does not sit on it. He sends a reply right back.

cards.question: Mordecai warns Queen Esther not to imagine something. What is it?

answers.text: That the palace will keep her safe
That the king will forget his decree
That Haman will change his mind

cards.question: Mordecai tells Esther that if she stays silent, the Jews will have no other hope of rescue.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: If Esther stays silent, what does Mordecai say will happen to her and her father's house?

answers.text: They will perish
They will be sent away
They will lose the crown

cards.question: Mordecai ends his reply to Esther with a question. What is he asking her to consider?

answers.text: Maybe she became queen for this very moment
Maybe the king never really trusted her
Maybe Haman has a plan against her too

cards.text: Here's how Mordecai puts it: "And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" Whew. Go ahead and read that one twice, friend. I'll wait.
Then Esther sends her reply to Mordecai. And this time, the queen is the one giving the instructions.

cards.question: Esther tells Mordecai to gather all the Jews who can be found in Susa. What does she ask them to do for her?

answers.text: Fast for her for three days
Stand outside the palace gate
Send letters to every province

cards.question: Esther says that she and her ___ will fast just as the Jews in Susa do.

answers.text: maidens
guards
officials

cards.question: After the three days of fasting, what does Esther say she will do?

answers.text: Go to the king even though it's against the law
Wait for the king to summon her to the court
Send Hathach in to speak to the king for her

cards.text: Then Esther says it: "And if I perish, I perish!" Friend, I need three alarms just to face a Monday, and this queen is ready to face the KING.

cards.question: Mordecai goes and does all that Queen Esther instructed him.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Mordecai's got his marching orders, and this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: The card says Haman 'got King Xerxes to seal a decree.' In Esther 3:10-12, the king gives Haman his signet ring, and the decree is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring. The text does not say the king sealed it himself.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The setup line 'And Mordecai is not the only one taking it hard' points to mourning like Mordecai's. That rules out the wrong answers on card 6 ('They gather together to fight back' and 'They pack up and leave the kingdom') before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks how many days Esther has not been summoned (thirty, seven or forty). This is exact wording from Esther 4:11 that the baker hasn't seen, and nothing earlier lets them reason it out. It is pure luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the thirty days the baker just answered on card 4 and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card. The joke could ride on a card that moves the passage forward.
'Mordecai does not sit on it. He sends a reply right back' adds speed the text doesn't give. Esther 4:13 only says 'he sent back to her this reply.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: This story card quotes the Esther 4:14 line the baker just answered on card 10, then reacts to it. It doesn't move the passage forward, so it is a recap card. The quote could go on a story card before the choice, or the reaction could ride on card 12.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
